chunks.text: Lord Ashford of Ashford House, Mayfair, has owned the Ashford Emerald for thirty years. On the evening of Thursday, 12 March 1891, he showed the stone to three guests in his study, locked the room, and sat down to dinner at eight o'clock. At half past nine he went to fetch the emerald for a toast to his late wife and found the study door still locked - and the glass case empty. Inspector Hollis has asked for your help before the household disperses. Establish who removed the emerald from the locked study, and prove it from the documents alone. Beware of confusing what a witness actually saw with what the witness merely supposed.
chunks.title: Case introduction: The Missing Emerald

chunks.text:
Ashford House, Mayfair, 2 March 1891.

My dear friends,

I should be honoured if you would dine with me on Thursday the twelfth, at eight o'clock sharp. Before dinner I shall show the Ashford Emerald to a few of you in my study, at a quarter past seven, since I intend to drink a toast to my late wife over the stone itself at half past nine. Dunmore will see that the household is in order. Kindly do not be late.

Yours sincerely,
Ashford
chunks.title: Dinner Invitation
chunks.author: Lord Ashford

chunks.text: KEY CABINET LEDGER - kept by Mr. Dunmore in the pantry, where he sits beside the cabinet. The cabinet is locked at all times. Its key is held by Mr. Whitmore alone. 6:00 PM - Cabinet opened by Mr. Whitmore. All spare keys present (Study, Library, Cellar, Conservatory). 7:35 PM - Lord Ashford informs me the study is locked with his own key. Spare Study key remains in cabinet.
chunks.title: Household Access Record — Key Cabinet Ledger
chunks.author: Mr. Dunmore, butler

chunks.text: Spare Study key remains in cabinet. 8:20 PM - Cabinet opened by Mr. Whitmore. Spare Study key taken out by him. 8:55 PM - Spare Study key returned to the cabinet by Mr. Whitmore. Cabinet locked. 9:35 PM - Lord Ashford rings; reports the emerald missing. Spare Study key found in its place. Note: the pantry clock was set by the hall clock at noon and agrees with it.
chunks.title: Household Access Record — Key Cabinet Ledger
chunks.author: Mr. Dunmore, butler

chunks.text:
Statement of James Whitmore, caretaker, to Inspector Hollis.

I took up my post in the front hall at eight o'clock when dinner was announced. I remained at that post until half past nine, when his lordship's bell was heard. I never touched the key cabinet that evening and I never entered the study. I did not see the emerald after the guests left the study at half past seven. I am a loyal servant of this house and I resent any suggestion otherwise.
chunks.title: Caretaker's Written Statement
chunks.author: James Whitmore

chunks.text:
Statement of Eleanor Ashford.

I came down at seven and joined my uncle's guests in the study at a quarter past. I saw the emerald in my uncle's hand. I assumed Richard had returned the emerald to its box before we left the study, since he was standing nearest the case. I did not watch him. I remained at dinner throughout, except for a minute at half past eight when I went to the drawing room for my fan.
chunks.title: Statement of Miss Eleanor Ashford
chunks.author: Eleanor Ashford

chunks.text:
Statement of Richard Hale.

Lord Ashford showed us the emerald at a quarter past seven. I looked at it in his hand through my glass. I never said that I had touched the emerald, and I did not. I sat at dinner throughout, except for ten minutes at twenty to nine when I took a cigar in the smoking room with Lord Ashford's leave. I regret that Miss Ashford should suppose otherwise.
chunks.title: Statement of Mr. Richard Hale
chunks.author: Richard Hale

chunks.text:
Statement of Clara Bennett.

I viewed the emerald in the study at a quarter past seven and left the room with the others at half past seven.
I did not enter the study again that evening. At about half past eight I left the dining room for the hall to fetch my shawl from the cloakroom. I called twice for a footman, but the hall was empty and nobody was at the front door. I returned to the table within eight minutes.
chunks.title: Statement of Miss Clara Bennett
chunks.author: Clara Bennett

chunks.text:
Memorandum found in Lord Ashford's desk.

Showed the emerald to E., R. and C. at a quarter past seven. I held it in my own hand throughout, and no one else handled the stone. I returned it to its case at about twenty-eight minutes past seven, shut the lid, and locked the study with my own key shortly after half past seven. The spare key is in the cabinet where it belongs.
chunks.title: Lord Ashford's Handwritten Memorandum
chunks.author: Lord Ashford

chunks.text:
Inspection of the study, Ashford House, by Inspector Hollis.

The study door was found locked with its key on Lord Ashford's watch chain. The lock bears no marks of force.
The window was latched from the inside and the dust on the sill was undisturbed. The glass case on the table has a hinged lid with a simple catch, and the emerald is missing from it. Messrs. Tompkins, locksmiths, confirm that only two keys to this door exist: his lordship's own and the spare in the key cabinet. Anyone who entered the room therefore did so with one of those two keys.
chunks.title: Study Inspection Report
chunks.author: Inspector Hollis

chunks.text:
Note brought to the kitchen door by an errand boy at ten past eight and handed to Mr. Whitmore by the kitchen-maid.

"J.W. - Our friend will wait at the mews gate at ten. Have the parcel ready. Say nothing to any lady or gentleman at table. - P."
chunks.title: Note Delivered Shortly Before the Disappearance
chunks.author: Unsigned, initial "P."

chunks.text: Eleanor Ashford, Lord Ashford's niece. Background: Orphaned at twelve and raised in her uncle's house. Lively, quick-tongued, and fond of fine dresses she cannot afford. Motive: Her allowance was halved in January and she owes a dressmaker and a card-club more than four hundred pounds. Relationship: Niece and dependent of the victim of the theft. Known whereabouts: At the dinner table throughout, except a short errand to the drawing room for her fan.
chunks.title: Profile of Eleanor Ashford

chunks.text: Personality: Talkative, defensive when pressed about money, prone to filling silences with guesses. She knows she is in debt and that servants gossip about it. She has not touched the emerald. She guessed that Richard had handled the stone because he stood nearest the case, but she did not actually watch him. Does not know: Where the spare study key was kept after seven o'clock. Anything about the caretaker's note.
chunks.title: Private knowledge of Eleanor Ashford

chunks.text: Questions: Where were you at half past eight? Did you leave the dining table? Where were you during dinner? Answer: I sat at table the whole of dinner, save for a minute at about half past eight when I ran to the drawing room for my fan. Ask the footman, he handed me back to my chair.
chunks.title: Eleanor Ashford on: Where were you at half past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Did you see Richard Hale return the emerald to its box? Did you actually see him touch the emerald? Answer: I did not watch him do anything of the kind. I merely assumed it, since he was standing nearest the case when we left the study. I cannot swear that I saw him touch it, no.
chunks.title: Eleanor Ashford on: Did you see Richard Hale return the emerald to its box

chunks.text: Questions: Do you need money? Why would you want the emerald? Are you in debt? Answer: My allowance is small, I do not deny it, and servants will talk. But a lady in want of money does not steal from the uncle who feeds her. I was at dinner.
chunks.title: Eleanor Ashford on: Do you need money

chunks.text: Questions: Who was the last person to hold the emerald? Who saw the emerald last? Answer: My uncle held it himself the whole time we were in the study. He put it back in its case and locked the door before we went in to dinner. That is the last I saw of it.
chunks.title: Eleanor Ashford on: Who was the last person to hold the emerald

chunks.text: Questions: Who do you suspect? What about Mr. Whitmore, Richard or Clara? Answer: I should not like to accuse anyone. Mr. Hale quarrelled with my uncle last month, and Mr. Whitmore has every key in the house. Beyond that I only know what I saw.
chunks.title: Eleanor Ashford on: Who do you suspect

chunks.text: James Whitmore, the household caretaker. Background: Eleven years caretaker at Ashford House. Keeps the cellar, the stables and the key cabinet. Respected, quiet, and always short of money since his brother's failed shop. Motive: He has debts to a money-lender in Whitechapel and knows every lock in the house. Relationship: Employee of Lord Ashford; keeper of the household keys. Known whereabouts: Claims to have stood at his post in the front hall from eight o'clock until half past nine.
chunks.title: Profile of James Whitmore

chunks.text: Personality: Formal, deferential, slow to answer, repeats his official duties when uneasy. SECRET (never admit): he took the spare study key from the cabinet at twenty past eight, opened the study, took the emerald and returned the key at five to nine. He received a note at ten past eight arranging a handover at the mews gate at ten. He will deny, deflect and cite his duties. He never confesses. Does not know: What Miss Bennett saw in the hall at half past eight.
chunks.title: Private knowledge of James Whitmore

chunks.text: Questions: Where were you at half past eight? Did you leave the hall during dinner? Where were you at 8:30? Answer: At my post in the front hall, sir, from eight o'clock until his lordship's bell at half past nine. I did not stir from it.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: Where were you at half past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Who has keys to the study? Who had access to the spare key? Who holds the key cabinet key? Answer: His lordship carries one study key. The spare hangs in the key cabinet in the pantry, and I alone carry the cabinet key. I did not touch the cabinet this evening.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: Who has keys to the study

chunks.text: Questions: Why does the access ledger show you took the spare key at twenty past eight? Why did Miss Bennett find the hall empty? Why does your statement contradict the ledger? Answer: Mr. Dunmore is an old man and the pantry clock runs slow. If I stepped to the pantry to give an order to the kitchen, I would hardly call that leaving my post. I never touched the study key.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: Why does the access ledger show you took the spare key at twenty past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Do you have debts? How long have you served? Why would you steal the emerald? Answer: Eleven years I have served his lordship and never a mark against my name. What I owe is my own affair and has nothing to do with this house.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: Do you have debts

chunks.text: Questions: What was the note delivered at ten past eight? Who is P? What is the mews gate? Answer: A tradesman's boy brought a note about a coal account, sir. I did not keep it. I know nothing of any mews gate arrangement.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: What was the note delivered at ten past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Who do you suspect? What about Miss Ashford, Mr. Hale or Miss Bennett? Answer: Miss Ashford is much in debt, so the servants say, and Mr. Hale quarrelled with his lordship. I do not like to carry tales about my betters.
chunks.title: James Whitmore on: Who do you suspect

chunks.text: Richard Hale, a business associate of Lord Ashford. Background: A shipping investor who partnered with Lord Ashford in two ventures. Dry, precise, and easily offended by imprecision. Motive: He quarrelled with Lord Ashford last month over a failed investment and still believes he was cheated. Relationship: Business associate of the victim of the theft. Known whereabouts: At table throughout dinner, except ten minutes in the smoking room at twenty to nine.
chunks.title: Profile of Richard Hale

chunks.text: Personality: Exact, irritable, answers literally and corrects other people's wording. He examined the emerald only as Lord Ashford held it, through his glass, at a quarter past seven. He never touched it. He is annoyed that Eleanor implied otherwise. He took a cigar in the smoking room from twenty to nine until ten to nine. Does not know: Who took the spare key. Anything about the note to the caretaker.
chunks.title: Private knowledge of Richard Hale

chunks.text: Questions: Did you touch the emerald? Did you return the emerald to its box? Miss Ashford says you returned it. Answer: I never said that I had touched the emerald, and I did not. Lord Ashford held it in his own hand while I looked at it through my glass. Miss Ashford is assuming.
chunks.title: Richard Hale on: Did you touch the emerald

chunks.text: Questions: Where were you at half past eight? Where were you during dinner? Did you leave the table? Answer: At table, save for ten minutes at about twenty to nine when I took a cigar in the smoking room, with his lordship's leave. The footman noted it.
chunks.title: Richard Hale on: Where were you at half past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Did you quarrel with Lord Ashford? Do you have a motive? Why are you angry with him? Answer: We disagreed over the Valparaiso shares last month. A disagreement is not a theft, Inspector. I would not risk my name for a green stone.
chunks.title: Richard Hale on: Did you quarrel with Lord Ashford

chunks.text: Questions: Who saw the emerald last? Who handled it? Who put it back in the case? Answer: Lord Ashford handled it throughout and put it back himself at about half past seven. I saw him do so.
chunks.title: Richard Hale on: Who saw the emerald last

chunks.text: Questions: Who do you suspect? What about the caretaker, Eleanor or Clara? Answer: I suspect nobody without evidence. I will say that the person who holds every key in a house is the person who ought to account for them.
chunks.title: Richard Hale on: Who do you suspect

chunks.text: Clara Bennett, a dinner guest. Background: A music teacher and a distant acquaintance of Lord Ashford's late wife. Observant, composed and a little shy among the wealthy. Motive: None apparent beyond her modest means; she met Lord Ashford only twice before. Relationship: Acquaintance and guest. Known whereabouts: At table except a short trip to the cloakroom for her shawl at about half past eight.
chunks.title: Profile of Clara Bennett

chunks.text: Personality: Polite, careful with words, states plainly what she saw and refuses to guess. She never entered the study after leaving it at half past seven. At about half past eight she went to the hall for her shawl, called twice for a footman and found the hall empty and nobody at the door. Does not know: Where Mr. Whitmore was at that time. Who held the keys.
chunks.title: Private knowledge of Clara Bennett

chunks.text: Questions: Did you enter the study? Did you go into the study after dinner began? Answer: I went into the study only once, at a quarter past seven, with the others. I did not enter it again that evening. I have never been in that room alone.
chunks.title: Clara Bennett on: Did you enter the study

chunks.text: Questions: Where were you at half past eight? Did you leave the table? What did you see in the hall? Answer: I went to the hall for my shawl at about half past eight. I called twice for a footman. The hall was empty, and there was no one at the door. I was back at table in eight minutes.
chunks.title: Clara Bennett on: Where were you at half past eight

chunks.text: Questions: Was Mr. Whitmore in the hall? Did you see the caretaker? Who was at the front door? Answer: I did not see Mr. Whitmore, or anyone. I can only say the hall was empty when I was in it. I do not know where he was.
chunks.title: Clara Bennett on: Was Mr. Whitmore in the hall

chunks.text: Questions: Who saw the emerald last? Who held it? Answer: Lord Ashford held it himself while we looked. He replaced it in its case and led us out. I did not see him lock the door, but I heard the key turn.
chunks.title: Clara Bennett on: Who saw the emerald last

chunks.text: Questions: Why are you here? Do you know Lord Ashford well? Do you need money? Answer: I teach the pianoforte and I met Lord Ashford twice before. I have no reason to take anything from him.
chunks.title: Clara Bennett on: Why are you here

chunks.text: Dr. Watson: "Holmes would first ask what each person actually saw, not what they supposed. Who truly handled the emerald, and who saw it last? Miss Ashford's guess is not evidence."
chunks.title: Watson hint 1

chunks.text: Dr. Watson: "There is a quarter of an hour at table when the hall was unobserved. Set the caretaker's own account of where he stood beside the dinner timeline and Miss Bennett's trip to the cloakroom."
chunks.title: Watson hint 2

chunks.text: Dr. Watson: "Since only two keys exist and his lordship kept his own, ask who could have used the other. Compare the caretaker's claim about the key cabinet with Mr. Dunmore's ledger. Whose claimed movements do not match the record?"
chunks.title: Watson hint 3
